question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution:
The correct answer is '**touched**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The context involves the king's wish for everything he contacts to transform into gold.
 
• The appropriate verb describes the act of making physical contact with objects.
 
• "**Touched**" (छूना) aligns with the narrative where the king's touch turns objects into gold.
 
• Other options ("**next felt**", "**kept**", "**left**") do not convey the specific action needed in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Once there was a king named Midas who was granted a **wish__ by Dionysus, the god of wine. For his wish, Midas asked that whatever he *__touched__* would turn to gold. Despite Dionysus’ efforts to prevent it, Midas pleaded that this was a fantastic wish, and so, it was bestowed. Excited about his newly-earned *(3)________*, Midas started touching all kinds of things, turning each item into pure gold. But soon, Midas became *(4)________*. As he picked up a piece of food, he found he couldn’t eat it. It had turned to gold in his hand. Hungry, Midas groaned, “I’ll starve! Perhaps this was not such an excellent wish after all!” Seeing his dismay, Midas’ *(5)________*daughter threw her arms around him to comfort him, and she, too, turned to gold. “The golden touch is no blessing,” Midas cried.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Next felt** (अगला महसूस किया): “Next felt” refers to subsequent feelings, inappropriate in this context.
 
• **Kept **(रखा हुआ): “Kept” refers to retaining possession, which doesn't fit the specific action of the story.
 
• **Left **(छोड़ा हुआ): “Left” means departed from or abandoned, which doesn't match the needed verb.
